statement: For every relative rounding model and finite binary tree of real pairs, if (depth+1)u < 1, the result obtained by rounding each leaf product and each internal addition is the exact sum of perturbed leaf products with the same tree shape. Each product changes by at most gamma(depth+1,u) times its absolute value, where gamma(k,u) = ku/(1-ku). The theorem concerns perturbations of products and asserts no separate perturbations of the input factors.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct_exists_perturbation
targets.statement: A model M consists of a real u = M.u with 0 <= u, a function r = M.round : R -> R, and the guarantee that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z) = z(1+delta). The delta may depend on z. M.mul(a,b) = r(ab) and M.add(a,b) = r(a+b). Tree(A) consists of finite ordered binary trees generated by leaf(a) for a in A and node(L,R) for two trees L,R; there is no empty tree. Depth is 0 at a leaf and 1 + max(depth(L),depth(R)) at a node. exactSum on Tree(R) returns the leaf value at a leaf and the exact real sum of the two recursive results at a node. For every such model M and every T in Tree(R x R), put d = depth(T). If (d+1)u < 1, where the natural number d+1 is cast to a real, there exists P in Tree(R) such that IsPerturbation(gamma(d+1,u), exactProductTree(T), P) and exactSum(P) = roundedDotProduct(M,T). For every natural k and real u, gamma(k,u) is defined as ((k as a real)u)/(1-(k as a real)u). IsPerturbation(B,A,P), for real B and real-valued trees A,P, is the inductively defined shape-preserving relation: at corresponding leaves x,y it requires |y-x| <= B|x|, and at corresponding nodes it requires the same relation on both left subtrees and both right subtrees. Hence P has exactly the ordered shape of T and, for each corresponding input leaf (a,b) and output leaf y, |y-ab| <= ((d+1)u/(1-(d+1)u))|ab|. exactProductTree(T) contains the exact products ab at its leaves. roundedDotProduct(M,T) evaluates r(ab) at each leaf and r(s_left+s_right) at each node, recursively. Its result therefore equals the exact sum of the leaves of P. The inequality ensures that the bound has a positive denominator. There is no balance, fixed leaf count, sign, or magnitude assumption on the input tree or its real entries.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.exactProductTree
constructions.description: A function E : Tree(R x R) -> Tree(R), defined for every input tree by mapping each leaf pair to its exact real product and preserving the ordered tree shape: E(leaf(a,b)) = leaf(ab), E(node(L,R)) = node(E(L),E(R)). It does not add leaf values. It supplies the reference tree whose leaves are perturbed in the target theorem.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree
constructions.description: For every model M and every T in Tree(R x R), this returns Q_M(T) in Tree(R), where Q_M(leaf(a,b)) = leaf(M.round(ab)) and Q_M(node(L,R)) = node(Q_M(L),Q_M(R)). It maps leaves using M.mul and preserves every node and the left/right shape; it performs no additions. Its result is passed to roundedSum by roundedDotProduct. The theorem does not identify this tree with the existential perturbed tree P. A model M consists of a real u = M.u with 0 <= u, a function r = M.round : R -> R, and the guarantee that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z) = z(1+delta). The delta may depend on z. M.mul(a,b) = r(ab) and M.add(a,b) = r(a+b).

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct
constructions.description: For every model M and every T in Tree(R x R), this is the real number roundedSum(M,roundedProductTree(M,T)). Here roundedSum(M,leaf(v)) = v and roundedSum(M,node(L,R)) = M.round(roundedSum(M,L)+roundedSum(M,R)). Equivalently D_M(leaf(a,b)) = M.round(ab) and D_M(node(L,R)) = M.round(D_M(L)+D_M(R)). It rounds each leaf product once and each internal addition once, following the supplied tree without rearrangement or balancing. Under (depth(T)+1)M.u < 1, the target theorem equates this value to exactSum(P) for some shape-preserving perturbation P of exactProductTree(T), with the stated relative bound on each product.

assumptions: A model M consists of a real u = M.u with 0 <= u, a function r = M.round : R -> R, and the guarantee that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z) = z(1+delta). The delta may depend on z. M.mul(a,b) = r(ab) and M.add(a,b) = r(a+b).

Tree(A) consists of finite ordered binary trees generated by leaf(a) for a in A and node(L,R) for two trees L,R; there is no empty tree. Depth is 0 at a leaf and 1 + max(depth(L),depth(R)) at a node. exactSum on Tree(R) returns the leaf value at a leaf and the exact real sum of the two recursive results at a node.

The theorem universally quantifies the model M and the input tree T in Tree(R x R). Its sole additional hypothesis is (depth(T)+1)M.u < 1, with depth(T)+1 a natural number cast to a real before multiplication. No other implicit mathematical parameters or hypotheses occur in the target type.
Input leaf components are arbitrary real numbers. No balanced-tree condition, particular floating-point format, rounding mode, or separate bound on either factor is supplied or assumed.
